# Kilotest

## What Kilotest is

Kilotest is an application that performs ensemble testing of web pages for front-end quality (i.e. accessibility, usability, and web standards, including HTML, CSS, ARIA, and WCAG) and reports the test results.

## What Kilotest does for language models

Kilotest is deployed on the public Internet as a service at `https://kilotest.com`. That deployment of Kilotest can test only web pages that can be accessed by its Testaro worker with a URL. Generally those are pages on the public Internet that are not protected by authentication or other access controls.

Without calling any tool, an LLM can, under some conditions, load web pages and use its knowledge to assess successes and failures of front-end quality. But such an assessment is almost always:

- expensive, substituting inference for deterministic rule application
- fragmentary, because of capability limitations, such as inability to run browsers and interact with web pages
- inaccurate, because of the tendency to replace missing information with hallucinations

To provide a more inexpensive, thorough, and accurate assessment, the agent could, in principle, ask an ensemble of specialized rule engines to test the page. However, selecting and running such rule engines and consolidating their results is itself expensive and difficult, and most available rule engines are not callable as MCP tools. Kilotest fills the gap between an LLM and rule engines. Kilotest:

- uses an ensemble of 12 rule engines to perform about 1,300 tests for front-end quality
- combines the reports of the rule engines into a single integrated report
- consolidates the rule violations into about 380 “issues” with a uniform naming system

The tools that report test results provide statistics and details at various levels of granularity specified by an agent to fulfill particular user requests.

## What Kilotest does **not** do for language models

The Kilotest tools are (currently) overkill for help in answering specific questions (e.g., “Is the heading structure of this page OK?”) when no report on the page is available, because in such cases you must wait up to a day before testing is completed.

Kilotest tools are thin on advice. They give you mostly facts and educated guesses about facts. The reporting uses rough heuristics to classify quality issues into 4 “priorities”, and some rule engines in the Kilotest ensemble include remediation advice when diagnosing rule violations, but Kilotest reporting does not otherwise advise you about the methods, sequences, urgency, or side effects of defect remediation.

## How Kilotest integrates methods

Testing for front-end quality requires a mixture of deterministic and inferential methods, because the standards of front-end quality vary in subjectivity. For example:

- The requirement that every element must have a landmark ancestor has no subjectivity, so it can best be tested deterministically.
- The requirement that images be marked up differently, depending on whether they are decorative or informative, has subjectivity, so its testing requires some inference.

The rule engines in the Kilotest ensemble take responsibility for determining whether each rule requires inferential testing and, if so, obtaining inference from an appropriate model.

## Kilotest versus other MCP servers

In the marketplace for MCP servers that test for front-end quality, all servers other than that of Kilotest leverage at most 3 rule engines, most often only `axe-core`. Most other MCP servers also require authentication. Kilotest leverages `axe-core` plus 11 other rule engines, and it does not require authentication.

For web pages that have not yet been tested, a single-rule-engine MCP can provide faster results than Kilotest. A tool running only the `axe-core` tests can complete its work in about 5 seconds. The testing tool of Kilotest usually completes its work in 2 to 4 minutes, because all 12 rule engines are run, and some of the tests involve navigation and interaction with the page and LLM inference.

For web pages about which reports are already available, Kilotest can provide faster results than a single-rule-engine MCP server, because Kilotest stores test results for subsequent retrieval. A retrieval from a Kilotest reporting tool can be completed in less than 2 seconds.

Kilotest results are more comprehensive than single-rule-engine MCP server results. Every rule engine provides limited coverage of front-end quality, so false negatives (missed defects) are more common with single-rule-engine MCP servers. This difference [has been documented in research](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2304.07591).

## How to use Kilotest

### Web UI

Kilotest offers a comprehensive suite of capabilities to users via its web UI:

- [Home page](https://kilotest.com/)
- [List all tested pages, with links to test results](https://kilotest.com/listPages.html)
- List all issues in one report, and all reports about the same page: `https://kilotest.com/listIssues.html/{reportID}`
- List all elements exhibiting one issue in one report: `https://kilotest.com/listViolators.html/{issueID}/{reportID}`
- List all diagnoses of one element exhibiting one issue in one report: `https://kilotest.com/listDiagnoses.html/{issueID}/{reportID}/{catalogIndex}`
- Get one full report in JSON: `https://kilotest.com/fullReport.json/{reportID}`
- [Request testing of a not-yet-tested web page](https://kilotest.com/requestNewTestForm.html)
- Request retesting of a web page: `https://kilotest.com/requestRetestForm.html/{reportID}`
- [List the operations available to Kilotest managers](https://kilotest.com/manage.html)
- [Get statistics about frequently reported issues across all pages](https://kilotest.com/listTopIssues.html)
- [Tutorial, “Accessibility testing strategies”](https://kilotest.com/tutorialWeb.html)
- [Tutorial, “Kilotest and AI”](https://kilotest.com/tutorialAI.html)

### API

In the specifications below, the term `report` refers to the records of one session in which a web page is tested. Each report has a unique identifier with a `YYMMDDTHHmm` initial and a 3-character final segment (example: 260503T0432-x9z).

Kilotest offers these tools:

- `listPages`
  - method: `GET`
  - purpose: list all tested pages, with links to test results
  - path: `/api/listPages`
  - caveat: Cached results are likely to be stale and should not be used
- `listIssues`
  - method: `GET`
  - purpose: list all issues in one report, and all reports about the same page
  - path: `/api/listIssues/{reportID}`
  - parameters
    - `reportID`: identifier of the report
  - source of parameters: response to a `listPages` request, or the history of reports about the page in the response to a `listIssues` request
- `listViolators`
  - method: `GET`
  - purpose: list all elements exhibiting one issue in one report
  - path: `/api/listViolators/{issueID}/{reportID}`
  - parameters
    - `issueID`: identifier of the issue
    - `reportID`: identifier of the report
  - source of parameters: response to a `listIssues` request
- `listDiagnoses`
  - method: `GET`
  - purpose: list all diagnoses of one issue exhibited by one element in one report
  - path: `/api/listDiagnoses/{issueID}/{reportID}/{catalogIndex}`
  - parameters
    - `issueID`: identifier of the issue
    - `reportID`: identifier of the report
    - `catalogIndex`: index of the catalog entry of the element (a string representation of an integer)
  - source of parameters: response to a `listViolators` request
- `questionDiagnosis`
  - method: `POST`
  - purpose: question or contest a diagnosis shown by `listDiagnoses`
  - path: `/api/questionDiagnosis/{issueID}/{reportID}/{catalogIndex}`
  - parameters
    - `issueID`: identifier of the issue
    - `reportID`: identifier of the report
    - `catalogIndex`: index of the catalog entry of the element
  - source of parameters: response to a `listDiagnoses` request
  - payload properties
    - `engineID`: identifier of the rule engine that produced the disputed diagnosis, shown in the `listDiagnoses` response
    - `ruleID`: identifier of the rule whose diagnosis is disputed, shown in the `listDiagnoses` response, or, if it is null, the description of the violation
    - `reason`: 20- to 1000-character explanation of why the diagnosis is questioned
- `getReport`
  - method: `GET`
  - purpose: get one full report in JSON
  - path: `/api/getReport/{reportID}`
  - parameters
    - `reportID`: identifier of the report
  - source of parameters: response to a `listIssues` request
- `requestNewTest`
  - method: `POST`
  - purpose: request testing of a not-yet-tested page
  - path: `/api/requestNewTest`
  - payload properties
    - `description`: description of the page to be tested
    - `URL`: URL of the page to be tested
    - `reason`: reason for testing the page
    - `reviewImmediately`: optional; `true` selects immediate review with immediate approval or rejection and immediate enqueueing if approved; `false` or omitted queues the request for review by management
- `requestRetest`
  - method: `POST`
  - purpose: request retesting of a page about which a report is available
  - path: `/api/requestRetest/{reportID}`
  - parameters
    - `reportID`: identifier of the latest report about the page
  - source of parameters: response to a `listIssues` request
  - payload properties
    - `reason`: reason for retesting the page
    - `reviewImmediately`: optional; `true` selects immediate review with immediate approval or rejection and immediate enqueueing if approved; `false` or omitted queues the request for review by management
- `requestFeature`
  - method: `POST`
  - purpose: request a feature improvement or a new feature
  - path: `/api/requestFeature`
  - payload properties
    - `feature`: description and motivation of the feature improvement or the new feature
- `awaitTest`
  - method: `POST`
  - purpose: wait for a job ordered via the `requestNewTest` or `requestRetest` tool with `reviewImmediately` set to `true` to complete; blocks until the report is ready, the job fails, or a maximum wait time elapses, then returns
  - path: `/api/awaitTest/{reportID}`
  - parameters
    - `reportID`: the report identifier returned by an immediately reviewed `requestNewTest` or `requestRetest` request
  - source of parameters: response to an immediately reviewed `requestNewTest` or `requestRetest` request
  - caveat: testing typically takes 2 to 4 minutes; sends no interim notices while waiting

## After a test, retest, or feature request

When you request a test or a retest:

- possible responses
  - acknowledgment of a successful request
  - error message
- possible Kilotest manager actions after a request
  - approval followed by the requested testing
  - rejection
- how to confirm approval
  - check test completion by calling `listPages` and looking for the page in the list
  - you advise the user to check in approximately 1 day for the test results on the Kilotest website, starting at `https://kilotest.com/listPages.html`

For immediate testing without waiting for review by management, set `reviewImmediately` to `true` in a `requestNewTest` or `requestRetest` request. That enqueues the job right away and returns a report identifier along with a question about whether to wait for completion. To wait, call `awaitTest` with that identifier; it blocks until the report is ready, the job fails, or a maximum wait time elapses. To check later instead, call `listIssues` with the same identifier.

An [OpenAPI specification for Kilotest](https://kilotest.com/openapi.yaml) is available.

## How to report results honestly to users

When you use Kilotest tools, you are free to perform any appropriate interpretation and condensation of the results, and action recommendations, for users. However, users expect the sources of facts and interpretations to be truthfully represented. Do not meld facts from Kilotest tools with interpretations of your own in a manner that misattributes your interpretations to Kilotest.

An example of a **poor** attribution is “Here are the results from Kilotest: …. The page is at risk of …. Among all the issues, … are critical and require immediate attention.” This attribution is poor because it incorrectly implies that Kilotest produced the interpretations and advice.

An example of a **good** attribution is “Kilotest reported these issues: …. On the basis of these results, I conclude that there is a serious risk of …, and, if you are responsible for maintaining the page, I recommend ….”
